expert_diagnosis: Yes Bank's crisis was caused by a combination of aggressive lending without adequate risk management, governance failures that allowed stressed assets to accumulate, and an inability to raise sufficient capital to restore solvency confidence. The systemic implications required regulatory intervention rather than a private-market solution. Root causes: asset-quality deterioration from poor risk management, capital inadequacy, liquidity confidence crisis, governance and risk-management failure, regulatory intervention risk, depositor confidence fragility.
expert_first_action: Regulator-led emergency capital reconstruction; immediate credible capital injection from state-backed institutions; liquidity backstop; board and governance reset with RBI oversight; transparent bad-loan recognition; protect depositor confidence with explicit government guarantee framework.
actual_decision: RBI and Indian authorities imposed moratorium on 5 March 2020. SBI-led reconstruction scheme implemented.
outcome_polarity: CONTAINED — systemic failure prevented by regulatory intervention
harmful_actions: Aggressive lending without adequate risk management created the stressed-asset problem
Governance failures allowed asset-quality deterioration to continue
Multiple failed private capital-raising attempts delayed resolution
Depositor confidence was allowed to deteriorate before intervention
beneficial_actions: RBI imposed moratorium preventing disorderly bank failure
SBI-led reconstruction with other banks provided credible capital injection
Depositors did not experience losses — confidence protected by intervention
Board and governance reset implemented under RBI oversight

actual_outcome: RBI imposed moratorium on Yes Bank on 5 March 2020. Yes Bank reconstructed with SBI and other Indian banks. SBI-led capital injection and RBI emergency liquidity provided. Depositors did not experience losses. Bank continued as reconstructed entity.
